correctness.rationale: Exact elimination y=V-x and exhaustive sine-range cases. Strict derivative monotonicity on tangent bands yields O(R) phase monotonicity components; counting phase-level crossings differs from density times total variation by O(R). The bounded primitive of |sin|-2/pi gives variation 2b R^2/pi+O(R) and hence the exact interior and boundary coefficients. The Jacobian determinant establishes O(R) critical interior roots and all-critical boundary roots. Analytic argument covers infinite R and all fixed real targets; finite checker only supports spot checks.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The original MM1 source asserts no fixed points for nonzero c and discusses forward attractor behavior. Neither implies the inverse image strip nor root-density growth. Even a statement of infinitely many inverse points without a rate would not imply the sharp coefficient, and inverse results for the alternate affine-in-x cosine maps do not imply MM1.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: An equivalent formulation would count roots of \(\sin(bx\cos(V-x))=s\) or inverse fiber multiplicity of MM1. The same-map full text covers different questions, and the closest cosine-memory variant has a different nonlinearity and hence no proved equivalence.

originality.rationale: All material reviewed primary texts were compared by their actual defining maps and claimed implications. The MM1 source treats fixed points and forward attractors, not the real-plane inverse-fiber asymptotic. Related studies employ different maps and do not dominate the proposed theorem. Direct searches did not locate equivalent MM1 quadratic counts, but a negative search is not a proof of unique priority. Closest indexed findings in private comparison covered different maps or different temporal-period properties.
residual_risks: An unindexed or inaccessible publication could already contain the same precise inverse-root asymptotic.
General oscillatory-root counting literature may provide a theorem that subsumes the calculation, though no checked source applies it to the specific map or critical boundary.
A differently normalized or modded state space changes the inverse problem and should not be silently equated with the real-plane theorem.

value.rationale: This computes a motivated exact inverse-state-reconstruction invariant for a published noninvertible planar map rather than an arbitrary slice: full attainable image, countably infinite fibers, sharp quadratic frequency of distinct sheets, factor-of-two critical boundary jump and asymptotic regularity. The coefficient is not a restatement of fixed-point/bifurcation results and distinguishes this map from maps with finite or linear inverse counts. The new mathematical information is usable without any unsupported downstream security claims.
